source.title: The Conflict Between Logic and Memory: Training Conditions for Optimizer-Dependent Rule Acquisition

record.tranche_reason: The study reports results on optimizer-dependent generalization, but mainly refines the gap claim: synthetic shallow networks show strong optimizer and training-permission effects, alongside shared failures under finite budgets. It does not test arbitrary-label memorization or the original natural-label generalization setup.
record.gate_note: Own results include same-distribution strict-parity test accuracy, optimizer comparisons, nuisance-freezing and masking interventions, and CIFAR-10 evaluations. Cited results from prior work are not included. The paper does not report fitting fixed random labels.
record.test_reason: The CIFAR-10 experiments directly compare Adam and momentum SGD held-out accuracy in two convolutional architectures under fixed learning-rate configurations. Adam performs worse in both. The synthetic rule-learning and intervention results concern settings outside V4's stated image and language benchmarks and do not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that acquired predictive relations depend jointly on the update rule and permitted adaptation. Nuisance freezing recovers a shared synthetic failure and removes a rare-mode optimizer advantage; strict parity and the mixed task retain finite-budget failures. They leave internal mechanisms, matched-parameter-count controls, target-necessity tests, and lower-rate Muon tuning unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses controlled synthetic rule-learning tasks and optimizer/intervention comparisons, plus CIFAR-10 performance. It does not reproduce the original random-label memorization and natural-label generalization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with optimizer, task, stage or mode, nuisance and background trainability, test-time masking, and learning-rate/checkpoint selection. In strict parity the transition varies with interaction order; Muon selects its lower tested learning-rate boundary from orders 7–12. CIFAR-10 optimizer ordering differs between Shallow-3 and VGG13-BN.

fits_no_version.finding: Freezing nuisance-connected weights raises fourth-stage accuracy to 68.47–70.56%, while post-training masking leaves it near chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Restricting nuisance adaptation can improve synthetic subgroup generalization despite continued nuisance exposure.

fits_no_version.finding: SGDM outperforms Adam and Muon on strict parity at orders ten and eleven; all approach chance at orders thirteen through twenty.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer-dependent synthetic parity learning varies with interaction order under the specified architecture, search grids, observation noise, and finite budget.

fits_no_version.finding: Background freezing improves all three optimizers and reduces the Muon–SGDM rare-mode gap from +11.99 to −0.49 percentage points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A synthetic rare-mode optimizer advantage depends on which background connections can adapt.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing every designated non-target input leaves mixed-task fourth-stage accuracy near chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing designated interference does not ensure recovery of the hardest synthetic subgroup.

record.problems: Strict-parity results use a finite budget and the same three seeds for learning-rate selection and test reporting; Muon selects the lowest tested learning rate at orders 7–12. CIFAR-10 comparison uses one seed, fixed learning rates, and no learning-rate sweep. Synthetic summaries generally have only three seeds. The authors note freezing greatly reduces trainable parameter count and matched-parameter-count controls are still needed. The recovered models were not tested with the designated fourth-order target block removed.
record.rows_left_out: The many other ordered cells in strict-parity Table 14 were grouped into the order 13–20 near-chance rows R16–R18; the paper's prose describes the full range as a shared result. Table 15's twenty-configuration overview is not fully row-expanded because the stage-level summary is an aggregate across configurations and does not provide uncertainty or all stage trajectories; the paper says those trajectories are not retained. The full CIFAR-10 optimizer matrix in Table 11 was reduced to SGDM/Adam comparisons per architecture; remaining configurations are not needed to map these versions.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting and paired natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.

Language benchmarks; learning-rate and decay-schedule tuning sweeps on CIFAR-10; broader hyperparameter tuning; matched training performance; switching optimizers; and decoupled-weight-decay recovery. The image comparison has one seed.
Large versus small batches under fixed epochs and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on dataset size, strength, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with alternative measures.
Removal of highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples, followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any version. Synthetic optimizer comparisons are informative extensions of the broader topic, but fall outside V4's expressly stated image and language scope. One seed and absent tuning sweeps restrict what the CIFAR-10 evidence establishes; these untested dimensions do not themselves warrant limits_scope verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: No fixed random-label training condition, arbitrary-label fit test, or paired random-label versus natural-label generalization result.
No width sweep or test-error comparison beyond the width needed for zero training error.
CIFAR-10 compares convolutional architectures and optimizer configurations, not convolutional versus fully connected networks or local connectivity.
No broad image-and-language benchmark suite; no comprehensive tuning comparison. Results concern specified synthetic tasks and one CIFAR-10 seed.
No batch-size sweep or comparison of large and small batches.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other perturbation-tolerance measure.
No removal of memorized examples or retraining comparison.

tranche.reason: The CIFAR-10 optimizer comparisons supply results on V4 in two additional architectures. The synthetic interventions do not establish a qualification of V4 within its specified benchmark scope.

reader_labels.condition: Specified shallow synthetic tasks, optimizer configurations, and training-selection procedures
reader_labels.reason: Optimizer outcomes differ by task and subgroup; the strict-parity comparison is finite-budget, Muon selects the lowest tested rate throughout orders 7–12, and CIFAR-10 uses one seed and fixed learning rates (R10–R18, R19–R26, R27–R30).
